answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the yarrow identifier and voids the later submissions, and therefore the operator pays for 57 runs and collects one. Because the harbor index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the lantern audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 57 answers need 57 separate inference runs with separate seeds. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
